item.title: Orbital_Engineering
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Orbital Engineering is a pivotal mid-to-late game technology that transitions your civilization from surface-based industry to a true spacefaring empire. It is the primary gateway to the Space tab’s most influential infrastructure.

Key Effects

Unlocking Orbital Engineering allows you to begin building and upgrading your orbital presence, specifically focusing on science and logistics:

  • Space Elevator: This is the most critical building unlocked by this tech. It drastically reduces the oil cost of launching space missions. Without it, the oil requirements for reaching the Farther Ring (like Jupiter) quickly become impossible to meet.
  • Satellite Radio: A Workshop upgrade that allows your Satellites to increase your Science cap. This is vital for reaching the science levels needed for Antimatter.
  • Navigation Relay: As we discussed earlier, this upgrade boosts Satellite effectiveness by +15%, further accelerating your Starchart and Science generation.

Unlock Requirements & Cost

  • Energy Impact: Each active Accelerator consumes 2 Watts of energy.
  • Storage Potential: Once the Energy Rifts upgrade is researched (via Dimensional Physics), Accelerators provide massive storage capacity for various resources, including catnip, wood, minerals, coal, iron, titanium, and gold.

Unlocked Technologies

Particle Physics is required to unlock two high-tier science branches:

  • Chronophysics: The branch dealing with time manipulation, Chronospheres, and reset preservation.
  • Dimensional Physics: The branch that unlocks the LHC (Large Hadron Collider) and Energy Rifts for expanded storage.

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

  • Enriched Uranium: Reduces the Uranium consumption of Reactors by 25% and provides a +25% Uranium production bonus to Quarries.
  • Railgun: A permanent military upgrade that increases the Catpower production of Hunter kittens by 25%.

Strategic Importance

Particle Physics marks the transition into the “Metaphysics” era. It is essential for generating the initial Unobtainium needed for space exploration; because Lunar Outposts consume uranium to produce unobtainium, players often rely on Accelerators (and trading with Dragons) to maintain their uranium supply until more efficient space-based uranium sources like Planet Crackers are built.

item.title: Paradox Theory
item.description:
Paradox Theory is a high-tier late-game science technology that acts as a fundamental gateway to advanced temporal mechanics and the “Shatter Engine” in Kittens Game.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 1,000,000 (1M)
  • Resource Requirements: 40 Time Crystals and 250 Void
  • Prerequisite: You must first research Void Space

Unlocked Upgrades and Structures

Researching Paradox Theory is required to unlock several critical late-game features:

  • Resource Retrieval (Time Tab): This is perhaps the most vital unlock; it allows you to retrieve 1% of your yearly resources (per level) whenever you shatter a Time Crystal. This is the foundation for infinite Time Crystal loops.
  • Chronocontrol (Void Space Structure): A structure that increases the duration (number of days) of a Temporal Paradox event. It also serves as the prerequisite for unlocking Chronosurge.
  • Distortion (Workshop Upgrade): This upgrade enhances the effectiveness of Chronocontrol, adding +3 days to the Temporal Paradox for every level of Chronocontrol built.
  • Void Resonator: An upgrade that allows the Order of the Void metaphysics bonus to trigger during a time skip. It also improves faith-to-worship production based on the number of resonators owned.

Strategic Importance

  • The Shatter Engine: Paradox Theory is the cornerstone of Phase 4 (Endgame) progression. By unlocking Resource Retrieval, it enables a self-sustaining cycle where shattering a Time Crystal generates enough Unobtainium to buy back more than one crystal through Leviathan trading.
  • Void Accumulation: Because it unlocks structures that extend the duration and effectiveness of Temporal Paradoxes, Paradox Theory is essential for farming the massive quantities of Void required for endgame buildings like Void Rifts.
  • Faith Scaling: Through the Void Resonator, players can continue to build their religious “Apocrypha” bonus while time skipping, ensuring that their production multipliers remain high even when bypassing thousands of years of normal game time.

  • Artisan (Trait): The Artisan kitten trait was also formerly known as the “Engineer” trait before being renamed to avoid confusion with the automation job.

Civil Service is an early-game science technology that focuses on village management and kitten specialization. It is essential for transitioning from a basic settlement to a more organized and efficient civilization.

Acquisition and Costs

  • Science Cost: 1,500 Science.
  • Prerequisites: You must first research Animal Husbandry.
  • Unlocks: Researching Civil Service provides the path to Currency and enables the Census feature.

The Census Feature

Unlocking Civil Service enables the Census section within the Village tab, providing detailed information about your population.

  • Kitten Identity: It reveals the names of your individual kittens (e.g., Lily, Oscar, Tails, Shadow).
  • Performance Monitoring: You can view how ably each kitten performs in their respective jobs.
  • Skill Levels: The Census tracks job experience, showing skill tiers such as Dabbling, Novice, Competent, and Master. These tiers provide multiplicative productivity bonuses for that specific job, ranging from 1% at Novice to 18.75% at Master.

Leader System

Civil Service grants the ability to assign a single kitten as the Leader of the village.

  • Assigning a Leader: A kitten can be made Leader by clicking the star icon next to their name in the Census.
  • Leader Traits: Each kitten is born with a random trait (e.g., Scientist, Artisan, Merchant) that provides a specific bonus only when they are assigned as the leader. For example, an Artisan leader increases your global craftRatio by +0.05, while a Scientist reduces the science cost of technologies by 5%.
  • Promotion and Rank: Leaders can be Promoted using gold and accumulated experience (Exp). Higher ranks significantly boost the kitten’s job production, and if you research the Republic policy, the leader’s rank provides a small production bonus to all other kittens in the village.

Strategic Importance

In the early game, Civil Service is primarily used to identify and assign kittens to jobs they are most skilled in, ensuring maximum resource yield. By promoting a leader who is highly skilled in a bottlenecked resource (like Woodcutting), you can effectively gain the equivalent of several extra kittens gathering that resource. Additionally, beelining this technology is required to unlock Currency, which is vital for starting international trade.

Calendar is the foundational science technology in Kittens Game, costing 30 Science to research. It is the primary prerequisite for the entire technology tree, unlocking Agriculture and the Time tab.

Functionality

Once researched, the Calendar provides essential information about the passage of time in your village:

  • Yearly Progression: It allows you to see the current day and season.
  • Village Age: It displays the total number of years your civilization has existed.
  • Time Tab: It unlocks the dedicated Time tab, where late-game temporal mechanics (like Redshift and Chronoforges) are managed.

The Time System

The game operates on a tick system, where one “tick” lasts 200 milliseconds. The units of time are defined as follows:

  • Day: 10 ticks (2 seconds of real-time).
  • Season: 100 days (3 minutes and 20 seconds).
  • Year: 400 days (13 minutes and 20 seconds).
  • Cycle: 5 years (1 hour, 6 minutes, and 40 seconds).
  • Millennium: 1,000 years (approximately 9 days and 6 hours).

Seasonal and Weather Mechanics

The calendar year is divided into four seasons—Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter—which directly affect catnip production.

  • Catnip Production: Fields receive a +50% boost in Spring and a -75% penalty in Winter.
  • Weather Modifiers: Starting at Year 4, seasons have a 35% chance to be “warm” (improving catnip yields) or “cold” (decreasing them further). In a Cold Winter, catnip production can drop by 90%.

Cycles and Late-Game Time

The game features ten five-year cycles named after space destinations: Charon, Umbra, Yarn, Helios, Cath, Redmoon, Dune, Piscine, Terminus (T-minus), and Kairo.

  • Looping: The full sequence of cycles repeats every 50 years.
  • Modifiers: With late-game Metaphysics (Numerology and Numeromancy), these cycles provide various production boosts or penalties to space structures and festivals.
  • Temporal Limits: In the 1000 Years challenge, the calendar stops advancing normally at year 500, requiring players to “shatter” Time Crystals to progress the year counter further.

  • Calciner: A complex industrial structure that consumes minerals and oil to produce iron and small amounts of Titanium. While slow, Calciners provide a steady domestic alternative to trading with Zebras for Titanium.

  • Breaking Resource Caps: The Alloy-tier storage upgrades are essential for reaching the high science and resource limits required for the Concrete Era and Mechanization.
  • Transition to Space: Chemistry is a mandatory step in the technology tree leading toward Electricity, Biology, and eventually the Rocketry needed for space missions.
  • Titanium Management: Strategic guides recommend building several Calciners immediately after researching Chemistry to begin accumulating the Titanium needed for advanced Workshop upgrades before domestic production becomes more efficient through later Metallurgy upgrades.
  • Village Progression: Players typically aim to acquire all Alloy buildings when they have approximately 90–100 kittens, using the expanded storage to push toward a population of 130+ for an efficient first reset.

  • Building Unlock: Enables the construction of Tradeposts, which reduce luxury resource demand and improve trading effectiveness.
  • Workshop Upgrade: Unlocks Gold Ore, which allows your Smelters to produce a small amount of gold (0.001 per tick) while they are active.

Gold (Primary Economic Currency)

Gold is the standard currency used for domestic improvements and international relations.

  • Production: Initially generated by Smelters with the Gold Ore upgrade. Later, Geologist kittens can produce it once the Geodesy workshop upgrade is purchased. In Iron Will mode, hunting also has a 25% chance of yielding gold.
  • Usage:
    • Trading: Used as a cost for discovering new civilizations and executing trades with certain races.
    • Promotion: Required to Promote kittens, which increases their rank and production bonuses.
    • Construction: A mandatory material for building Temples, Tradeposts, and Mints.
    • Religion: Essential for purchasing high-tier Order of the Sun upgrades and executing faith resets via Apocrypha.

Prestige Currencies (Resets)

These are earned by resetting the game and provide permanent, stacking benefits for future runs.

  • Karma: Earned if you have more than 35 kittens at reset. It primarily increases Kitten Happiness, which provides a global production bonus.
  • Paragon: Earned if you have more than 70 kittens at reset (1 point for every kitten over 70). It provides a global production bonus and increases resource storage caps.
  • Burned Paragon: Regular Paragon can be “burned” to provide a smaller but separate production boost that is highly effective during the Dark Future (Year 40,000+).

Special and Late-Game Currencies

  • Catpower: While technically a resource, it functions as a currency for Sending Explorers (1,000 Catpower) and initiating Hunts (100 Catpower).
  • Blackcoin: A speculative cryptocurrency bought and sold from Leviathans in exchange for relics. Its price fluctuates over time.
  • Time Crystals: A rare currency used to purchase advanced temporal technologies like Chronospheres and to skip years via time shattering.

item.title: Void Space
item.description:
Void Space is a high-tier endgame science technology and a dedicated section in the Time tab that marks the transition into Phase 3 of Kittens Game, focusing on advanced temporal mechanics and the use of the Void resource.

Technological Unlock

Furthermore, building a “Void Seed” through numerous Void Rifts is a primary strategy for reaching the massive Unobtainium caps (over 8 billion) required for self-sustaining positive resets in the late game.

Core Effects

Deploying satellites provides immediate global benefits to your science and resource generation:

  • Science Cap: Each satellite improves the Science capacity of Observatories by 5%. This bonus can be further increased by 10% if the Militarize Space policy is enacted.
  • Starchart Production: Satellites generate a base of 0.005 starcharts per second. While slower than Research Vessels, they are often the first automated source of starcharts available to the player.
  • Energy Consumption: By default, each satellite consumes 1 Watt of energy.

Workshop Upgrades and Synergies

The utility of satellites is greatly enhanced through various Workshop upgrades:

  • Hubble Space Telescope: Increases the starchart production of all buildings, including satellites, by 30%.
  • Solar Satellites: Transforms satellites from energy consumers into producers, causing each one to generate 1 Watt instead of consuming it.
  • Satellite Navigation: This is a critical mid-game upgrade where every active satellite reduces the starchart cost of crafting Trade Ships by 1.25% (capped at a 75% discount).
  • Satellite Radio: Every active satellite provides a +0.5% bonus to the maximum culture and culture production of Broadcast Towers.

Cyclical and Environmental Impacts

The effectiveness of your satellite network fluctuates based on the current temporal cycle:

  • Cath Cycle: Provides a +100% bonus to satellite starchart production and the science bonus they provide to observatories.
  • Kairo Cycle: Imposes a -25% penalty to these same bonuses.
  • Challenges: Building at least one satellite is a mandatory goal for completing the Energy challenge. In the Black Sky challenge, their starchart production is reduced based on the number of times you have completed the challenge.

Strategic Importance

The primary utility of Agriculture is ensuring Winter survival.

  • Season-Proof Production: While Catnip Fields suffer a massive production penalty during Winter (typically -75% or up to -90% in cold winters), the catnip generated by Farmers is not affected by seasons or weather.
  • Winter Reallocation: Strategic guides recommend reallocating most of your kittens to the Farmer job temporarily when Autumn ends to ensure your food production remains positive throughout the Winter months.
  • Storage Caps: Without Barns, your wood and mineral caps will be too low to purchase higher-tier buildings or research advanced technologies.

Technology Path and Progression

Agriculture serves as a mandatory gate for several essential branches of the technology tree:

  • Immediate Path: Agriculture is the direct prerequisite for Mining (which unlocks the Workshop) and Archery (which unlocks the Hunter job).
  • Build Order: Efficient progression usually involves researching Calendar → Agriculture → Mining → Archery in rapid succession.
  • Enhancements: Farmer productivity can be further improved through Workshop upgrades like Mineral Hoes (+50% boost) and Iron Hoes (+30% boost).

Transition to Late Game

While Agriculture is vital early on, its relative importance shifts as you progress. In the mid-to-late game, players often replace Aqueducts with Hydro Plants and Pastures with Solar Farms to prioritise energy production over raw catnip bonuses. Eventually, once you have accumulated enough Paragon and Karma, your base production bonuses may become high enough that you only need a single Farmer to sustain a large population.

item.title: Animal Husbandry
item.description:
Animal Husbandry is an early-game scientific technology that is essential for transitioning from basic survival to infrastructure development and more advanced resource management. It is unlocked after researching Archery and costs 500 Science.

Core Buildings and Effects

Researching Animal Husbandry unlocks two primary structures focused on managing the colony’s food economy and rare resources:

  • Pastures: These buildings cost 100 Catnip and 10 Wood. Each Pasture provides a -0.5% reduction in catnip demand per kitten.
  • Unicorn Pastures: These structures cost 2 Unicorns and provide a smaller -0.15% reduction in catnip demand. Additionally, they automatically generate 0.001 unicorns per tick.

The demand reduction from both building types is vital for surviving Winter, as it decreases the constant food burden imposed by the kitten population. However, this reduction is subject to strict diminishing returns and is hard-capped at 50%.

  • Unicorn Tree: Animal Husbandry remains relevant to religious progression through the Unicorn Tree. Workshop upgrades like Unicorn Selection (unlocked via Genetics) further improve the effectiveness of Unicorn Pastures by 25%.

2. The Cryptotheology System (Phase 3)

Cryptotheology is described as the system that provides “Insights into the mysteries of time and space” and focuses on the Time, Relics, and Void mechanics of the game. It is the defining feature of the Phase 3 (End Game) of Kittens Game .

The core purpose of the system is to purchase permanent, powerful structures using Relics and Void, which often scale with the player’s Transcendence Tiers (TT).

3. Buildings and Upgrades

Cryptotheology buildings purchased persist across resets and are unlocked sequentially based on your Transcendence Tier (TT), which is bought with Epiphany.

Building/Upgrade Primary Cost Transcendence Prerequisite Primary Effect
Black Obelisk 100 Relics TT 1 Improves your Solar Revolution bonus cap by +5% per Transcendence Tier.
Black Nexus 5,000 Relics TT 3 Improves relic production from two sources: Refining Time Crystals (1 + (Black Nexus * Black Pyramid) relics) and Relic Station upgraded Space Beacons.
Black Core 10,000 Relics TT 5 Increases the Sorrow (Black Liquid Sorrow or BLS) limit by +1% .
Event Horizon 25,000 Relics TT 7 Increases global resource storage ratio by +10%. This stacks additively with Void Rifts and multiplicatively with other storage bonuses [6, 8].
Black Library 30,000 Relics TT 9 Improves Codex Leviathanianus scaling by +2% per library, further boosted by Unicorn Graveyards .
Black Radiance 37,500 Relics TT 12 Increases the alicorn corruption rate based on the amount of Sorrow (BLS) and the number of Black Radiances.
Blazar 50,000 Relics TT 15 Improves Chronomancy and Unicornmancy by 2.5%, Time Impedance by 10%, and Resource Retrieval effectiveness by 2% [9]. Blazars are vital to a Time Crystal engine .
Dark Nova 75,000 Relics, 7,500 Void TT 20 Provides a +2% global energy production bonus.
Mausoleum 50,000 Relics, 12,500 Void, 10 Necrocorn TT 23 Unlocks the ability to purchase Pacts.
Holy Genocide 100,000 Relics, 25,000 Void TT 25 Unlocks the Post Apocalypse challenge upon reset .

4. Strategic Role and Goals

  • Relic Conversion: Cryptotheology provides direct use for Relics, which are primarily created by refining Time Crystals (25 TCs = 1 Relic).
  • Late-Game Gate: Once a player can build Eludium Huts easily, they are ready for the unicorn/time crystal phase. The next major goal is to maximize the Solar Revolution bonus (capped at 1000% before Cryptotheology upgrades) and reach Transcendence Tier15 . Reaching TT 15 is necessary to purchase the Blazar, which is considered vital to a Time Crystal engine [10, 15].
  • Boosting Persistence: Cryptotheology buildings are key to late-game scaling. For example, Black Obelisks boost the cap of the Solar Revolution bonus.
  • Challenges: The ultimate building, the Holy Genocide, is required to unlock the Post Apocalypse challenge.

Primary Unlocks and Effects

The research of Astronomy unlocks essential buildings and the resources needed for advancement:

  1. Observatory Building: Astronomy unlocks the Observatory building.
    • Observatories boost Science production by +25% and increase your Max Science by +1000.
    • They also improve the chance of getting science and starcharts from external events, increasing the Astronomical Event Chance by +0.2% and the Automatic Event Observation Chance by +1%.
  2. Starcharts: Astronomy enables starcharts . Starcharts are categorized as an Uncommon Resource, found by observing rare astronomical events.
  3. Navigation: Astronomy unlocks the next key technology, Navigation. Navigation subsequently unlocks other crucial techs like Architecture, Physics, and Geology.
  4. Policy/: Astronomy, in conjunction with the Diplomacy policy, unlocks foreign Policy/ such as Knowledge Sharing and Cultural Exchange.

Strategic Importance

Astronomy is strategically important because it unlocks the mechanism to acquire starcharts, a resource necessary for building Trade Ships and ultimately leading to the discovery of the Zebras, who trade essential resources like Titanium and Iron.

Before researching Astronomy, you may occasionally see a message about “astronomical events” in your log, which allows you to click a button to earn Science. However, once you research Astronomy, observing these events will yield starcharts. Because starcharts are a major bottleneck for trade expansion, building many Observatories is prioritized to increase the rate of seeing and automatically clicking on these meteors.

The goal upon reaching this point is to build enough Observatories to get starcharts at a “healthy rate” before focusing heavily on Steel production.

Navigation enables the crafting of Trade Ships.

  • Trade Ships are critical for reaching the Titanium era, as they are the major upgrade for obtaining more Titanium through trading with Zebras.
  • Crafting a Trade Ship initially requires 100 Scaffold, 150 Plate, and 25 Starchart.

2. Building Unlocks

Navigation unlocks the Harbour building.

  • Harbours provide substantial increases to storage capacity for several key common resources:
    • Catnip: +2500.
    • Wood, Minerals, Iron, Coal, Gold, and Titanium storage limits are all increased.
    • The Expanded Cargo upgrade (unlocked by Navigation) further increases Harbour capacity by 1% per trade ship, up to a limit of 225%.

3. Workshop Upgrades

The technology also unlocks several important Workshop upgrades focused on resource efficiency and trade relations:

  • Caravanserai: This upgrade improves race relations by giving each Tradepost a flat 0.35% chance decrease to the hostile event probability and a 0.175% increase to the friendly event probability.
  • Titanium Axe: Improves Woodcutters’ output by 50%.
  • Astrolabe: Improves Observatory effectiveness.
  • Titanium Reflectors: Increases the maximum science storage bonus derived from Libraries/Data Centers based on the number of Observatories you have.

Navigation acts as a necessary gateway, like plotting a course to a new continent, enabling the building of the ships (Trade Ships) and port infrastructure (Harbours) needed to access lucrative resources (Titanium and Iron) from distant, often hostile, civilizations.

item.title: Nuclear Fission
item.description:
Nuclear Fission is a pivotal technology research in the late mid-game, crucial for advancing your industrial infrastructure, especially regarding energy production, titanium refinement, and unlocking access to Uranium trade.

Unlocking and Cost

  • Prerequisite: Nuclear Fission is unlocked after researching Electronics.
  • Cost: Researching Nuclear Fission requires 150,000 Science and 100 Blueprint.

Key Unlocks and Effects

Nuclear Fission provides both industrial capacity and scientific progression:

  1. Building Unlocked: Reactor

    • It unlocks the Reactor mega-structure.
    • The Reactor costs 3500 Titanium, 5000 Plate, 50 Concrete, and 25 Blueprint.
    • It provides a substantial +5% Global Production bonus.
    • It generates +10 Energy but consumes Uranium at a rate of 0.001 per Tick.
    • It also increases maximum Uranium storage by +250.

  2. Workshop Upgrades

    • Nuclear Smelters: This upgrade allows existing Smelters to produce Titanium at a rate of 0.0015 per tick. This provides a domestic source for the critical resource Titanium.
    • Reactor Vessel: This upgrade improves the ship potential for expanded Harbour capacity, specifically increasing the Harbour capacity limit by 5% per active Reactor past the 225% limit.

  3. Technology Progression

    • Nuclear Fission unlocks two major scientific pathways: Nanotechnology and Particle Physics.

Researching Biochemistry opens access to the next scientific field and provides a crucial Workshop upgrade:

  1. Next Technology: Biochemistry unlocks Genetics.
  2. Workshop Upgrade (Biofuel Processing): The research enables the Biofuel Processing Workshop upgrade. This upgrade provides a significant functional benefit to the Bio Lab building (unlocked by Biology).
    • Bio Labs, with the Biofuel Processing upgrade, can automatically convert catnip into oil.
    • This conversion consumes 5 catnip per second (or 1 catnip per tick), and uses 1 Watt of Energy.
    • In exchange, the Bio Lab produces 0.10 oil per second (or 0.02 oil per tick),.

Strategic Significance

Biochemistry plays a critical role in mitigating the oil production bottleneck in the late mid-game, particularly for players facing resource constraints or engaging in specialized runs:

  • Oil Supply: By enabling Bio Labs to convert catnip to oil, Biochemistry helps players utilize massive catnip surpluses to generate industrial fuel. Oil is a common resource needed for structures like Oil Wells, Calciners, and Kerosene production,,.
  • Kerosene Production: The Oil Processing technology, unlocked by Rocketry, enables the production of Kerosene. Kerosene is a crucial fuel for space missions (like Dune Mission and Moon Mission) and the Orbital Array,,. A steady supply of oil via Biofuel Processing is fundamental to maintaining Kerosene production velocity.
  • Production Scaling: The subsequent research unlocked by Genetics is the GM Catnip upgrade, which further improves the oil yield from Bio Labs by 60%,.
  • Run Planning: Due to the high science and compendium costs, the Biology research pathway (which leads to Biochemistry) is sometimes advised to be skipped in initial runs until players can easily craft Alloy.

Key Unlocks and Effects

Researching Mechanization provides crucial industrial capabilities and new construction materials:

  1. Resource Unlocked (Concrete): Mechanization enables the production of concrete. Concrete is a highly important crafted material necessary for advancing housing and storage infrastructure.
  2. Building Unlocked (Factory): This technology unlocks the Factory building. Factories are essential for late-game industrial scaling and boosting crafting efficiency.
  3. Kitten Job Unlocked (Engineer): Mechanization enables the Engineer job, allowing kittens to automate crafting processes in the Workshop.
  4. Workshop Upgrades: Mechanization unlocks critical efficiency upgrades in the Workshop:
    • Concrete Pillars: A storage upgrade that increases the maximum capacity of several resources (wood, minerals, iron, coal, gold, and titanium) from Barns, Warehouses, Harbours, and Mints by $+5%$.
    • Pumpjack: This upgrade improves the effectiveness of Oil Wells by $45%$ and enables their automation, although Oil Wells will then consume 1 Watt of energy each.

Mechanization is a major checkpoint on the path to high-tier buildings and population management:

  • Concrete Era: This research is necessary for achieving Concrete Huts. Concrete Huts require a tremendous amount of titanium and grant a major reduction in the price ratio of Huts, making population expansion cheaper.
  • Technological Progression: Mechanization directly unlocks the next tier of science, Electronics.
  • Endgame Focus: While the costs for Mechanization are high, players are advised to pre-emptively grind for the huge amount of titanium required for the subsequent Concrete upgrades, as this process will often provide most of the blueprints needed to research Mechanization itself through trade bonuses.

3. Strategic Role

Metal Working is a critical early-game step for expanding resource production and moving toward industrialisation:

  • Iron Production: This technology is essential because Minerals become increasingly important for advanced buildings. Metal Working allows you to put your minerals to work by building Smelters to create Iron.
  • Production Trade-off: While beneficial for accessing Iron and Gold, building Smelters requires converting minerals and wood, so players must bear in mind that creating Iron will reduce your Wood and Mineral stores.
  • Lumber Mill Prerequisite: The subsequent technology that boosts wood production, the Lumber Mill, requires Iron for construction, meaning Metal Working must be researched first.
  • Iron Will Mode: In Iron Will mode, after Gold Ore is researched, Hunting produces Gold, which is important since kittens cannot be employed as Geologists for gold production in this mode.

Metal Working is a mandatory step in the “Basic Resource Rotation” necessary for establishing a strong economic foundation by processing basic resources into advanced components.

Metaphysics is a core technology research and an associated system of permanent, prestige-based upgrades unlocked in the late mid-game of Kittens Game. These upgrades are crucial because, once purchased using Paragon, they carry over across game resets, enabling significantly faster progress in subsequent runs.

1. Unlocking and Requirements

  • Prerequisite Technology: Metaphysics is unlocked by researching Physics.
  • Cost: Researching the technology costs 55,000 Science and 5 Unobtainium.
  • Activation: The technology itself enables the Metaphysics system, but upgrades within the system must be purchased using the prestige currency Paragon.

2. Strategic Role and Benefits

Metaphysics upgrades are the primary tool for achieving geometric scaling in subsequent runs, as they provide permanent bonuses that do not disappear upon reset.

The most effective upgrades generally fall into three categories:

A. Price Ratio Reduction (Economic Scaling)

These upgrades decrease the price ratio of structures in the Bonfire tab, meaning the cost of buying subsequent buildings grows much slower. This is one of the most significant benefits, allowing players to build many more structures (and gain more production/population) before hitting storage caps.

The recommended sequence for these early upgrades is:

  1. Enlightenment (5 Paragon): Reduces all price ratios by 1%.
  2. Golden Ratio (50 Paragon): Reduces price ratios by approximately 1.618%.
  3. Divine Proportion (100 Paragon): Reduces price ratios by approximately 1.777%.
  4. Vitruvian Feline (250 Paragon): Reduces price ratios by 2%.
  5. Renaissance (750 Paragon): Reduces price ratios by 2.25%.

B. Progression and Quality of Life (QoL) Upgrades

These upgrades accelerate key production bottlenecks and progression hurdles:

  • Diplomacy (5 Paragon): Causes races to be discovered earlier (unlock year reduced from 5 to 1) and with better standing. This is recommended to get early in the game.
  • Chronomancy (25 Paragon) and Astromancy (50 Paragon): These are useful early QoL upgrades. Chronomancy multiplies the daily chance of meteors and astronomical events by 1.1x, while Astromancy doubles the astronomical event chance and observatory effectiveness (for event chances and auto success rates). This helps mitigate the early starchart bottleneck.
  • Venus of Willenfluff (150 Paragon) and Pawgan Rituals (400 Paragon): These significantly boost the speed at which kittens arrive (75% faster and an additional 150% faster, respectively), which is vital for quick paragon farming runs.
  • Anachronomancy (125 Paragon): Crucially, this upgrade ensures that Time Crystals and the Chronophysics technology are saved across resets. This is mandatory before seriously engaging in Time Crystal acquisition.

C. Endgame Systems and Prestige

These upgrades enable or significantly boost endgame systems related to time, religion, and unicorns:

  • Megalomania (10 Paragon): Unlocks Markers and Black Pyramids, which are key to starting the Unicorn/Time crystal Era and engaging the Leviathan trade partner. Megalomania is necessary for refining Unicorn Tears into Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS).
  • Numerology (50 Paragon) and Numeromancy (250 Paragon): These enable Cycles to affect space production (Numerology) and grant bonuses during festivals based on the current cycle (Numeromancy). The Redmoon cycle, when combined with Numeromancy, provides a significant boost to Unobtainium production.
  • Order of the Void (75 Paragon): Causes all faith production to also produce 10% of that amount in Worship.
  • Codex Upgrades (Vox, Logos, Agrum): These increase the crafting ratio for manuscripts, compendiums, and blueprints, respectively. Although they are costly, they are not recommended for newer players as their bonuses are minimal compared to the price ratio reductions.

3. Progression Strategy

Metaphysics dictates the early Paragon Grind phase (Phase 1/Early Game). A player’s goal in the first few runs is to accumulate enough Paragon (by resetting with over 70 kittens) to buy the most impactful Metaphysics upgrades.

A suggested goal is to aim for 60 Paragon on the first reset to buy Diplomacy, Enlightenment, and Golden Ratio, and then 100 Paragon on the second run to buy Divine Proportion. Once price ratio reductions are secured, you can focus on later QoL upgrades like Chronomancy and Astromancy, and eventually, the endgame technologies like Anachronomancy and Megalomania.

Researching Exogeology unlocks several crucial elements and leads directly to the next phase of high-tier crafting:

  • Next Science Tier: It unlocks Exometallurgy (formerly Advanced Exogeology), which is the science required to enable the crafting of Eludium.
  • Housing Upgrade: It unlocks the Unobtainium Huts upgrade. This upgrade requires 200K Science, 350 Unobtainium, and 15K Titanium, and reduces the Hut price ratio by 25%.
  • Storage and Production Upgrades: It unlocks several specialized Workshop upgrades:
    • Unobtainium Reflectors: These improve telescope reflectors, increasing the maximum science bonus gained from Observatories by an additional 2% per Observatory.
    • Unobtainium Drill: This improves the effectiveness of Geologists.
    • Hydro Plant Turbines: This upgrade makes Hydro Plants 15% more effective (increasing energy output from 5 Wt to 5.75 Wt).
    • Storage Bunkers: This is a vital storage upgrade that increases the maximum storage limit for wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium from Warehouses, Barns, Harbors, and Mints by 20%. The storage bunkers upgrade requires 25K Science, 500 Unobtainium, and 1250 Concrete.

3. Strategic Importance (The Unobtainium Era)

Exogeology marks the beginning of the “Unobtainium Era” and is a step towards the “Eludium Era” [6, 7].

  • Storage Bottleneck: Acquiring the Storage Bunkers upgrade, which Exogeology unlocks, is recommended once you reach 500 Unobtainium capacity [8]. This helps address storage limits, which are a major bottleneck in the game [9, 10].
  • Late-Game Progression: After achieving Concrete Huts (unlocked by Mechanization) [11], players should aim for Unobtainium Huts, which are unlocked by Exogeology, before attempting to reset the game, as this marks a major population and storage milestone [12].
  • Eludium Goal: The ultimate goal after Exogeology is to research Exometallurgy to craft Eludium. This typically requires significant Unobtainium storage (e.g., 1000 Unobtainium capacity via multiple Moon Bases or a Cryostation) to reach the capacity needed for Eludium Huts [7].

If you are following the recommended progression path, you should continue resetting once you can reach the Unobtainium Huts until you have acquired the Renaissance Metaphysics upgrade (750 Paragon), which makes reaching Unobtainium Huts easier in subsequent runs [7].

Researching the Steel technology immediately enables several important upgrades in the Workshop:

  • Resource Production:
    • Steel Axe: Permanently increases Woodcutter output by 50%.
    • Coal Furnace: Allows Smelters to produce Coal (0.005 coal/tick) while operating.
    • Deep Mining: Allows Mines to produce Coal (0.003 coal/tick).
    • High Pressure Engine: Reduces the Coal consumption of Steamworks by 20%.
  • Storage and Hunting:
    • Reinforced Warehouses: Increases the storage space for common resources (wood, minerals, coal, iron, gold, and titanium) from Warehouses, Barns, Harbors, and Mints by 25%.
    • Steel Armour: Provides a permanent +0.5 Hunting bonus to increase resource yields from hunting.

4. Strategic Importance and Use

Steel is a required component for many major buildings and subsequent technological advancements:

  • Buildings Requiring Steel:
    • Steamworks: The crucial automation building (requires 65 Steel).
    • Mansion: A later housing upgrade.
    • Quarry: A resource building (requires 125 Steel).
    • Calciner: An industry building.
    • Data Center: An upgraded Science building (requires 100 Steel).
  • Crafting Requirements: Steel is needed to craft Gears and is a component in making Alloy.
  • Conflicting Advice:
    • The “Monstrous Advice” column recommends prioritizing Steel first among the three post-Writing technologies, specifically to gain the useful upgrades that strengthen your economy, before moving to Machinery and Philosophy.
    • Conversely, the walkthrough advises considering Steel a “specialist Tech” and suggests prioritizing Philosophy because it is cheaper and maintains forward progression.
  • Resource Management: In early runs, after acquiring the initial Workshop upgrades unlocked by Steel, players are often advised to ignore coal and let it max out, dedicating their iron production to building Lumber Mills and Observatories, as Steel quickly becomes a bottleneck for future construction.

Steel acts as the foundation for the next stage of industrial complexity, marking the point where your civilization transitions from basic resource gathering to automated production and advanced crafting. This reliance on Steel leads directly into the Machinery era, as Steel is required for the construction of the Steamworks.

  • The Hunter Job: This technology enables you to assign kittens as Hunters, who produce 0.06 catpower per tick.
  • The Hunt System: Once you have accumulated 100 catpower, you can send your kittens on a hunt. This is the primary method for obtaining rare resources like Furs and Ivory, and it offers a 5% chance to find Unicorns.
  • Technological Branching: Archery is the mandatory prerequisite for Animal Husbandry, which leads to housing improvements and the “Unicorn Tree”.
  • Zebra Buildings: For advanced players, Archery unlocks Zebra-specific structures including the Zebra Outpost, Zebra Workshop, and Zebra Forge.

The effectiveness of the systems unlocked by Archery can be drastically improved through specific Workshop upgrades:

  • Catpower Production: You can boost the rate at which Hunters generate catpower using the Composite Bow (+50%), Crossbow (+25%), and Railgun (+25%).

In the early game, there is often a choice between researching Archery or Mining. Archery is the strategic pivot point for the specialised “Iron Will” (IW) mode, where the player progresses without any kitten housing:

  • Zebra Discovery: In IW mode, Zebras serve as the primary source of catpower (acting as passive Hunters) and begin to appear only after Archery is researched.
  • The Reset Loop: A common strategy involves researching Archery and then immediately resetting the game. Doing this while in Iron Will increases your maximum Zebra limit for the next run.
  • Prestige Setup: Players often perform 6 to 10 of these short “Archery resets” to accumulate 50–60 Zebras. This provides a permanent, efficient catpower source that bypasses the need to feed kittens, significantly accelerating mid-game economic stability.

item.title: Drama and Poetry
item.description:
Drama and Poetry is a mid-game technology that moves your civilisation from basic resource management into cultural and temporal optimization. It is primarily known for unlocking the Festival mechanic and the Brewery building.

Costs and Prerequisites

Because of its high requirement for a specific crafted resource, it is often seen as a significant hurdle for new players.

  • Science Cost: 90,000.
  • Resource Cost: 5,000 Parchment.
  • Prerequisite: Researching Acoustics.

Unlocked Mechanics

  • Festivals: Once researched, you can spend resources to hold a festival that lasts for one game year (400 days, or 800 real-time seconds).
    • Kitten Growth: Festivals are the primary way to double the arrival speed of kittens (from ~0.16 to 0.32 kittens per second), which is essential for reaching the population thresholds needed for Paragon.
    • Numeromancy Synergies: If the Numeromancy Metaphysics upgrade is researched, holding a festival grants massive global production multipliers based on the current Cycle (e.g., x2 Unobtainium in Redmoon, x2 Science in Piscine, or x2 Catpower in Cath).
  • Brewery: A building that enhances the effectiveness of your festivals.
    • Cost: 1,000 Wood, 750 Culture, 5 Spice, and 375 Parchment.
    • Effects: Provides a +1% bonus to Festival Happiness and the Festival Cycle Bonus, while increasing Festival Kitten Speed by +0.1%.
    • Upkeep: Each active Brewery consumes -1 Catnip and -0.1 Spice per tick.

Strategic Utility

  • Early Game Skip: Experienced players recommend skipping this tech on your first few runs because the 5,000 Parchment cost is considered “waaaay too expensive” to be useful when your economy is still weak.
  • Mid-to-Late Game Priority: It becomes vital when you start pursuing Unobtainium farming or rapid Paragon grinding. In short runs (approx. 30 minutes), players often stack multiple festivals to ensure kittens fill housing as fast as it is built.
  • Parchment Grinding: To prepare for this tech, it is recommended to stockpile at least 7,500 Parchment so you can afford the research and immediately hold several festivals to see the benefit.

The term Philosophy in Kittens Game refers to a critical mid-early game technology that unlocks essential progression paths, as well as a subsequent category of Policy/ that govern societal beliefs regarding luxury and endurance.

Here is a detailed breakdown of the Philosophy technology and its associated Policy/:

1. Philosophy as a Technology

Philosophy is a specialist science research that becomes available after you have researched Writing.

Detail Information Source
Cost 9,500 Science.
Prerequisite Writing.
Key Unlock (Tech) Theology.
Key Unlock (Building) Temple.
Main Effect Enables the creation of compendiums.

Compendiums

Compendiums are a crucial craftable resource unlocked by Philosophy.

  • Purpose: They are composite documents required for subsequent technological advancement. Every compendium created provides +10 to max science, though this bonus cannot exceed the maximum science cap derived from buildings.
  • Crafting: A compendium is crafted in the Workshop by combining 50 Manuscripts and 10,000 Science.

Strategic Importance

There is conflicting advice in the sources regarding when to prioritize the Philosophy technology:

  • Walkthrough Advice: The “Kittens Game” walkthrough suggests that among the three technologies unlocked by Writing (Philosophy, Machinery, and Steel), you should choose Philosophy to start because it is the cheapest and keeps you on the main path of advancement.
  • Expert Advice: The “Monstrous Advice” column recommends prioritizing Steel and Machinery first to strengthen your economy and automate manuscripts, and then taking Philosophy last, specifically so you will have ways to make all the manuscripts needed to build Temples.

After researching Philosophy, you will immediately face a “fair bump” because the subsequent technology, Theology, has “fairly steep requirements” involving manuscripts and culture.

2. Philosophy as a Policy Category

Philosophy is one of the four categories of Policy/ (along with Government, Foreign, and Environment) that defines your society’s path in certain areas.

The main policy choices unlocked once the Philosophy technology has been researched are Stoicism and Epicureanism.

Stoicism vs. Epicureanism

Both Policy/ cost 2,500 Culture and lock out the other choice.

Policy Description & Effect Prerequisite & Progression
Stoicism Teaches endurance without complaint. Effect: Halves the consumption of luxury resources (Fur, Ivory, and Spice are consumed 50% slower), and reduces Brewery consumption by 25%. This policy unlocks the choice between Frugality and Rationing later on.
Epicureanism Believes pleasure is the highest good. Effect: Luxury resources provide 11% happiness each (instead of the base 10%). This policy unlocks the choice between Carnivale and Extravagance later on.

Expert advice suggests preferring Epicureanism for the extra happiness boost, noting that Stoicism addresses a problem (managing luxury consumption) that should ideally be manageable by the time the policy is available through hunting and trade upgrades. Choosing either Epicureanism or Stoicism is a prerequisite for subsequent philosophical choices like Rationality or Mysticism.

item.description:

Costs and Prerequisites

  • Science Cost: 140,000.
  • Resource Cost: 80 Blueprints.
  • Prerequisite: You must have researched Electronics.

The Hydro Plant Pivot

Researching Robotics allows you to upgrade your Aqueducts into Hydro Plants.

  • Effect: Each Hydro Plant provides +5 Energy (which can be increased to 5.75Wt with the Hydro Plant Turbines upgrade).
  • Strategic Risk: This is described as a “high-risk” infrastructure pivot. While Hydro Plants are vital for powering your growing industrial base, upgrading them causes you to lose the +3% catnip production bonus provided by Aqueducts.
  • Recommendation: Do not upgrade until your titanium production is robust and you are certain your catnip production (boosted by Paragon and Karma) can sustain the population without the Aqueduct bonus.

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Robotics provides access to several upgrades that drastically improve industrial output and kitten efficiency:

  • Robotic Assistance: Reduces the catnip consumption of working kittens by 25%. This is essential for managing the “happiness liability,” where high happiness levels normally cause massive spikes in food demand.
  • Steel Plants: This causes Calciners to automatically convert 10% of their iron output into Steel (at a 100:1 ratio).
  • Rotary Kiln: Dramatically enhances Calciner efficiency, making them 75% more effective at producing Iron and 3 times as effective at producing Titanium.
  • Factory Robotics: Improves Engineer effectiveness by increasing the “know-how” of Class 1, 2, and 3 Engineers.

Resource and Progression Unlocks

  • Tankers: Robotics enables the crafting of Tankers in the Workshop. Each Tanker increases your maximum Oil capacity by 500. While useful for reaching the high oil caps required for space missions, some strategies suggest prioritizing steel-grinding for Oil Wells instead, as Tankers can be expensive in the early-space era.
  • Artificial Intelligence: Robotics is the mandatory prerequisite for the Artificial Intelligence science, which leads to AI Cores and the Gigaflop era.

Strategic Significance

Robotics represents the point where your civilization begins to “replace” marginal agricultural bonuses with high-density energy generation and automated manufacturing. By reducing food demand and automating steel and titanium production, Robotics allows you to focus on the massive resource requirements of the Space era and the transition toward Antimatter.

Unlocked Technology

Unlocked Workshop Upgrades

Researching this technology provides access to three highly impactful upgrades that drastically improve your energy balance and production:

  • Space Manufacturing:
    • Effect: This allows your village’s Factories to provide a production bonus to space-based structures based on 75% of your factory craft ratio.
    • Impact: It specifically increases the Space Bonus from Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays by 3.75% per factory (this increases to 4.5% if you also have the Factory Logistics upgrade). This is essential for scaling Unobtainium production to the levels required for the deep endgame.
  • Cold Fusion:
    • Effect: Increases the energy output of Reactors by 25%.
    • Impact: This provides a flat boost of +2.5 Watts per active Reactor, significantly easing energy bottlenecks.
  • Cryocomputing:
    • Effect: Reduces the energy consumption of Data Centers by 50%.
    • Impact: Each Data Center’s power drain is reduced from 2 Watts to 1 Watt, allowing you to maintain massive science storage without overwhelming your power grid.

Strategic Importance

Superconductors is often considered the threshold for the “Positive Reset” loop. By unlocking Space Manufacturing, players can finally farm enough Unobtainium to build the high number of Chronospheres needed to carry over more resources than they spent during a run. Additionally, the combined effects of Cold Fusion and Cryocomputing allow for a much larger industrial and scientific infrastructure to be powered simultaneously, which is critical for supporting energy-intensive late-game buildings like AI Cores and Entanglement Stations.

Unlocked Technology and Upgrades

Researching this technology unlocks the Void Space science and provides access to three powerful Workshop upgrades:

  • Chronoforge: Unlocks the “Chronoforge” section in the Time tab. This allows you to combust (shatter) Time Crystals to skip ahead to the next spring, advancing the calendar year instantly. This is the foundation of the late-game “Shatter Engine,” used to rapidly generate antimatter and resources.
  • Tachyon Accelerators: A massive storage upgrade for Accelerators, increasing the capacity they provide for catnip, wood, minerals, iron, coal, gold, and titanium by 500%.
  • Chronoengineers: An efficiency upgrade that allows Engineers to continue performing crafts during a time skip (provided you have Resource Retrieval levels).

Strategic Importance

Tachyon Theory is primarily used as a gateway to the Endgame Reset Loop. By unlocking the Chronoforge, it allows you to manipulate time to stay within beneficial cycles, such as the Redmoon cycle, which provides a massive boost to Unobtainium production.

Furthermore, it is a required prerequisite for Void Space, which is necessary to attempt the Atheism Challenge and to begin collecting Void, a resource essential for reaching the game’s theoretical limits.

This structure represents the process of melting Yarn’s ice and oxygenating its atmosphere to support life.

  • Cost: 25 Antimatter, 5,000 Uranium, and 5,000 Kerosene.
  • Effect: Each station increases your maximum kitten population by +1.
  • Synergy: Every unit of Hydroponics you own provides a +1.0% bonus to the kitten capacity of your Terraforming Stations, allowing them to eventually house more than one kitten each.

Tectonic (Centaurus System)

This structure involves ripping open the planet near the star Centaurus to harvest magma energy.

  • Cost: 600,000 Science, 500 Antimatter, and 75,000 Thorium.
  • Effect: Each Tectonic provides +25 Energy.
  • Upgrades: Every level of Molten Core (requires Exophysics) improves Tectonic energy production by an additional 5%.
  • Challenge Goal: Building at least one Tectonic is a requirement for completing the Energy Challenge.

Strategic Utility

Terraformation is a cornerstone of the Endgame Paragon phase. By “Terraforming Yarn,” players can build a vast amount of housing (potentially support up to 60,000 kittens), which is essential for generating massive amounts of Paragon per reset. Additionally, Tectonic structures provide the high-density energy required to power late-game facilities like AI Cores and Entanglement Stations without relying solely on ground-based reactors.

item.title: Theology
item.description:
Theology is a pivotal science technology in Kittens Game that marks a significant transition point in the civilization’s progression, particularly by introducing the Religion system.

Prerequisites and Cost

Theology is unlocked in the Science tab after researching Philosophy. Reaching this science is noted as a “fair bump” because it has steep requirements that force the player to establish production systems for specialized resources.

The cost to research Theology is:

  • Science: 20,000
  • Manuscripts: 35

This Manuscripts requirement involves grinding out resources, as Manuscripts must be crafted from Parchment (derived from Furs, acquired through Hunting) and Culture (generated by buildings like Amphitheatres and Temples). Overcoming this hurdle will likely take a long time.

Effects and Unlocks

Upon successful research, Theology provides several immediate unlocks crucial for advancing the civilization:

  1. New Resource and Production: Theology unlocks the generation of Faith, a new expendable resource used primarily in the Religion tab.

    • It enables the Priest profession. Kittens assigned as [Priests] ( /job/priest/) initially produce 0.0015 faith per tick.
    • It enables Temples to generate Faith, specifically at a rate of 0.0015 faith per tick per Temple.

  2. New Systems:

    • It unlocks the Religion tab.
    • It unlocks the ability to build Temples (which were already unlocked by Philosophy, but Theology makes them functional for Faith).
    • It unlocks the Order of the Sun, the religious upgrade system.

Importance in Progression

Theology is crucial because it gates access to the next stages of technological and religious development:

  • Religious Upgrades: It allows the player to start investing Faith in religious upgrades by using the “Praise the sun!” option to gain Worship. Religious upgrades, such as Scholasticism (which lets Temples boost Science maximum capacity by +500) and Sun Altar (which contributes to Happiness), affect areas outside of the Religion system.
  • Scientific Path: Theology unlocks the pathway to the next major sciences, Astronomy and Cryptotheology.
  • Manuscript Reliance: Once Theology is researched, future sciences, such as Astronomy (requiring 65 Manuscripts), will also require Manuscripts, making efficient Culture and Parchment production essential for continued technological growth.

  • Unlocked Upgrades: Researching this technology enables the thorium resource and unlocks the Thorium Reactors, Thorium Drive, and Quantum Dot Cells workshop upgrades.

Acquisition and Production

There are two primary ways to obtain Thorium once the technology is researched:

  • Workshop Crafting: You can craft thorium from Uranium.
    • Recipe: 250 Uranium yields 1 Thorium.
    • Efficiency: Kittens with the Chemist trait provide a specific crafting bonus (+0.075) to thorium yield.
  • Trading: Once you have reached a Level 5 Embassy with the Dragons, you can trade with them for thorium.
    • Exchange: They buy 250 Titanium and have a 50% chance to sell 1 unit of Thorium (with a 25% range).

Key Workshop Upgrades

Thorium is a required input for several high-tier upgrades that optimize your village and space travel:

  • Thorium Reactors:
    • Effect: Increases the energy output of your Reactors by 25% (+2.5 Watts).
    • Upkeep: While active, each Reactor consumes -0.05 thorium per tick.
    • Strategy: Players are advised to turn off this upgrade after purchasing and only activate it when time-skipping to generate antimatter, as the thorium drain can quickly deplete stockpiles.
  • Enriched Thorium: Costs 500,000 Thorium; it reduces Reactor thorium consumption by 25%.
  • Thorium Drive: Costs 100,000 Thorium; it significantly increases space travel speed, dividing travel times by 50.
  • Quantum Dot Cells: Costs 1,000 Thorium; it improves Solar Farm efficiency throughout the year, particularly providing a 30% boost in spring and autumn.

Space Missions and Infrastructure

Thorium is a major mission-gate resource for reaching the farthest points of the Helios system:

  • Umbra Mission: 15,000 Thorium.
  • Charon Mission: 35,000 Thorium.
  • Centaurus System Mission: 50,000 Thorium.
  • Furthest Ring Mission: 75,000 Thorium.
  • Tectonic (Centaurus structure): Requires 75,000 Thorium to build.

Endgame Strategic Utility

In the late-game “Iron Will” 40k runs, thorium becomes a critical bottleneck for reaching high antimatter caps. To reach a 5,000 Antimatter capacity for relic stations, players often need around 34 Heatsinks, which carries a total cost of approximately 526,000 Thorium. Because of these massive costs, managing your uranium-to-thorium crafting chain is vital for entering the Relic and Antimatter eras.

item.title: Writing
item.description:
Writing is a foundational mid-game science that costs 3,600 Science and requires Engineering as a prerequisite. It is widely identified as the first major “speedbump” or bottleneck in the game, marking the transition into a phase where progression relies on complex resource management rather than simple manual gathering.

Technological and Structural Unlocks

Researching Writing provides access to essential tools for cultural and industrial expansion:

  • Parchment: Writing enables the crafting of Parchment in the Workshop. Parchment is produced using Furs, which are primarily obtained through the Hunt system using Catpower.
  • Amphitheatres: This technology allows for the construction of Amphitheatres, which are the earliest buildings used to generate Culture. Crucially, they also mitigate unhappiness caused by population growth, which is vital for maintaining kitten productivity.
  • Science Progression: Writing is the mandatory prerequisite for the Philosophy, Machinery, and Steel technologies.
  • Register: This Workshop upgrade becomes available, allowing leaders to manage jobs by prioritizing kittens with higher experience.

Strategic Utility

The primary role of Writing is to establish the “Cultural Engine” required for the mid-game. Parchment is the mandatory base material for Manuscripts, which are required in large quantities to unlock critical sciences such as Theology, Astronomy, and Navigation.
